transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-06
Time: 14:00 - 14:45 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Leo Grant (Redwood SE), Amit Patel (Timberbrook CTO), Sara Lemos (Timberbrook Head MLOps), Diego Ruiz (Timberbrook Procurement)

Auto Summary (auto gen, may be rough): discuss renewal, add APAC/EU on-prem pilot, ask for security docs, run perf bench, agree next steps and owners.

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll give about 30 minutes of updates then a run-through of next steps; Leo is joining to talk benchmarks and security.
00:14 Amit Patel: Thanks Maya, appreciate it, busy week so keep tight. We're trying to decide between extended dedicated commit or split dedicated + private onprem for EU/APAC for residency.
00:30 Leo Grant: Quick clarifying q, when you say onprem do you mean Private deployment package, like VPC plus on-prem appliance, or full air-gap?
00:45 Sara Lemos: More like customer-managed VPC and an on-prem package in our EU DCs, maybe air-gap later. Need KMS/HSM support, audit logs.
01:05 Maya Chen: Yep that's what Redwood Private supports — private control plane with customer KMS hooks. minor note, our docs sometimes say Dedicate... um Dedicated pools, yes.
01:20 Diego Ruiz: From procurement side timeline, we need to know commitment sizes and pricing by next Friday to align with Q1 PO cycle.
01:37 Leo Grant: Understood. For latency tradeoffs, Dedicated in region gives lowest p99, but if you go on-prem you'll get local latency but there's more ops overhead. We can do a hybrid.
01:55 Amit Patel: Hybrid sounds right. Can Redwood do automatic routing/fallback between on-prem and hosted if the on-prem nodes have a spike?
02:10 Leo Grant: Yes, we have smart routing that can failover to compatible model variants or hosted pool; there is a small cold-start cost if KV cache isn't warm — we call it KV cache warmup.
02:30 Sara Lemos: That warmup concern is real for low-latency interactive flows. What's the realistic p50/p95 difference?
02:45 Leo Grant: For typical transformer workloads we're seeing p95 in-region Dedicated ~80-120ms token time for short sequence, on-prem might be 60-100ms depending on local infra; fallback to hosted adds 100-300ms depending on network and model variant. These are ballpark — we'll run your workload.
03:05 Amit Patel: Sounds reasonable, please put those in the benchmark. Also we'd like to quantify unit-cost impact if we use quantized models vs full fp16; our ops lead wants to know quality delta.
03:30 Maya Chen: Good call — we'll include cost/perf tradeoffs with quantization options.
03:42 Leo Grant: Also note we can suggest batching and KV prefix caching policies that save tokens, but that may increase tail latency for single-shot requests.
03:58 Diego Ruiz: On the procurement ask, do you do multi-year discounts or just annual?
04:10 Maya Chen: We offer tiered reserved pricing — 1-year and 3-year commitments with different uplift rates. We'll send a sample spreadsheet with run-rate models.
04:25 Amit Patel: We'll need a 3-year view to show CFO.
04:32 Sara Lemos: Security questions: SOC2, ISO, and can you integrate with our Azure Key Vault / Hashi HSM? Also audit log retention.
04:50 Leo Grant: Yes SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certs are available, we integrate with common KMS providers — we'll share the exact integration notes; audit logs retention configurable depending on plan.
05:05 Maya Chen: I'll attach the compliance pack and KMS guide.
05:12 Amit Patel: Another thing — do you support per-route quotas and token-level cost breakdown for our finance team?
05:25 Maya Chen: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-model breakdown, and per-route dashboards; we can create an example view for Timberbrook.
05:40 Sara Lemos: Great. Pilot scope: want to run a 4-week on-prem pilot in EU, and a parallel Dedicated reserve in us-east for 50% of traffic, then measure. Can Redwood provision staging nodes for us?
06:00 Leo Grant: We can provision staging capacity and give you a small reserved pool for baseline tests, yes. We'll coordinate on infra sizing — need sample qps and sequence lengths.
06:15 Amit Patel: We'll share sample traffic and a 2-day subset of logs.
06:25 Leo Grant: Perfect. For benchmarks we'll run throughput and latency with both quantized and fp16 variants; we'll also test model fallback to hosted and measure cache warmup times.
06:40 Diego Ruiz: Contractually we need SLAs for uptime and latency SLOs to present to procurement — can you include that in the pricing doc?
06:52 Maya Chen: We'll include SLA language and options — dedicated capacity has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; private deployments have a slightly different operational model.
07:05 Sara Lemos: Any notes on egress costs if we route cross-region? That matters for us.
07:18 Leo Grant: Yes egress will be called out; for Private on-prem there may be less egress since traffic is local, but fallback to hosted will incur network egress. We'll model egress in the cost sheet.
07:33 Amit Patel: Competitors we've evaluated: BigCloudAI (their multi-region infra is strong) and Orion Inference (cheaper but less mature on governance).
07:48 Maya Chen: Good to know; we'll try to show cost/perf comparisons in the SPREAD.
08:00 (short silence)
08:15 Maya Chen: Ok quick recap before we go into details — agreed: Timberbrook wants 1) Pricing by 2026-12-10, 2) Security docs by 2026-12-09, 3) SE benchmark by 2026-12-17, 4) pilot kickoff week of 2026-12-20. Anyone disagree?
08:33 Amit Patel: No, sounds good.
08:38 Diego Ruiz: timeline fits our PO cycle.
08:43 Sara Lemos: We also need a short Regen testing window to validate model quality after quantization.
08:53 Leo Grant: We'll include quality evals tied to your prompt set; can flag regressions and show tradeoffs.
09:05 Maya Chen: Great. Specifics on the pilot: who owns infra tasks?
09:12 Amit Patel: We'll assign an infra lead after the PO, but for now Sara will be primary for MLOps coordination.
09:20 Sara Lemos: Yep I'll be primary.
09:24 Leo Grant: I'll draft a short pilot runbook and share it with Sara for review — includes staging sizing, run commands, and validation checklist.
09:36 Maya Chen: Any final procurement constraints Diego?
09:40 Diego Ruiz: Need contract terms for data residency and indemnity clauses; we'll review once we have pricing.
09:47 Maya Chen: We'll flag those in the contract template.
09:52 (cross-talk, typing)
10:05 Maya Chen: Ok last bit — can Leo run a short smoke test in our lab with a synthetic workload to double-check latency numbers?
10:18 Leo Grant: Yes will do, but to match your production we need the sample logs Amit mentioned.
10:25 Amit Patel: Sending them by EOD today.
10:30 Maya Chen: Perfect, we'll follow up with calendar invites for kickoff and a doc bundle.
10:40 (wrap)

Meeting end: 14:45 UTC

Transcript notes: transcription sometimes substitutes product terms (e.g., "Dedicate" for Dedicated, "KV cache warm up" appears variably). Some names abbreviated; timestamps approximate.

Referenced artifacts/links: pricing spreadsheet (to be sent), security pack (SOC2/ISO PDF), KMS integration notes, pilot runbook (draft)
notes: Customer strongly leaning to hybrid approach. Procurement timeline tight; 3-year view requested for CFO. SE to validate latency & quantization quality impact. Redwood to provide security docs and pricing spreadsheet.
